library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(labelled)
library(haven)

# Load all files from data/input/
file_list <- c(
  "wave_one_lsype_young_person_2020.tab",
  "wave_two_lsype_young_person_2020.tab",

  "ns9_2022_main_interview.tab"
)

# Load each file
w1 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[1]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)
w2 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[2]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)

w5 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[5]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)

w7 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[7]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)
w8 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[8]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)
w9 <- read_delim(file.path("data/input", file_list[9]), delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Loaded all files.\n")
cat("W1 nrow:", nrow(w1), "\n")
cat("W9 nrow:", nrow(w9), "\n")

# Merge all datasets by NSID using full_join
df <- w1 %>%
  full_join(w2, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w3, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w4, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w5, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w6, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w7, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w8, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(w9, by = "NSID")

cat("Merged dataset nrow:", nrow(df), "\n")

# Helper function to map missing values to standard codes
map_missing <- function(x) {
  # Map based on label meaning
  # -999, -998, -997, -995 -> -2 (schedule not applicable / script error / information lost)
  # -99 -> -3 (not asked / not interviewed)
  # -94 -> -8 or -2 (depends on label)
  # -92 -> -9 (refused)
  # -91 -> -1 (not applicable)
  # -999 -> -2
  # -100, -97 -> depends on label
  
  result <- x
  
  # Map specific codes based on metadata
  # Wave 1: -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
  # Wave 2: -998 = Interviewer missed question -> -2, -997 = Script error -> -2, 
  #          -995 = Missing history section data -> -2, -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3,
  #          -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1, -1 = Don't Know -> -8
  # Wave 3: -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
  # Wave 4: -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1, -1 = Don't know -> -8
  # Wave 5: -1 = Don't know -> -8
  # Wave 6: -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
  # Wave 7: -91 = Not applicable -> -1
  # Wave 8: -9 = Refused -> -9, -8 = Don't know -> -8, -1 = Not applicable -> -1
  # Wave 9: no missing values
  
  result
}

# Function to harmonize a sex variable based on its wave-specific missing codes
harmonize_sex <- function(x, wave) {
  result <- x
  
  if (wave == 1) {
    # -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -99] <- -3
    result[is.na(result) & x == -92] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
  } else if (wave == 2) {
    # -998 = Interviewer missed question -> -2, -997 = Script error -> -2,
    # -995 = Missing history section data -> -2, -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3,
    # -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1, -1 = Don't Know -> -8
    result[is.na(result) & x == -998] <- -2
    result[is.na(result) & x == -997] <- -2
    result[is.na(result) & x == -995] <- -2
    result[is.na(result) & x == -99] <- -3
    result[is.na(result) & x == -92] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -1] <- -8
  } else if (wave == 3) {
    # -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -99] <- -3
    result[is.na(result) & x == -92] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
  } else if (wave == 4) {
    # -99 = YP not interviewed -> -3, -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1, -1 = Don't know -> -8
    result[is.na(result) & x == -99] <- -3
    result[is.na(result) & x == -92] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -1] <- -8
  } else if (wave == 5) {
    # -1 = Don't know -> -8
    result[is.na(result) & x == -1] <- -8
  } else if (wave == 6) {
    # -92 = Refused -> -9, -91 = Not applicable -> -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -92] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
  } else if (wave == 7) {
    # -91 = Not applicable -> -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -91] <- -1
  } else if (wave == 8) {
    # -9 = Refused -> -9, -8 = Don't know -> -8, -1 = Not applicable -> -1
    result[is.na(result) & x == -9] <- -9
    result[is.na(result) & x == -8] <- -8
    result[is.na(result) & x == -1] <- -1
  }
  
  # Convert remaining NAs to -3 (not asked / not interviewed)
  result[is.na(result)] <- -3
  
  return(result)
}

# Harmonize all sex variables
# Wave 1 (Age 14): W1sexYP
df$W1sexYP_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W1sexYP, 1)

# Wave 2 (Age 15): W2SexYP
df$W2SexYP_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W2SexYP, 2)

# Wave 3 (Age 16): W3sexYP
df$W3sexYP_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W3sexYP, 3)

# Wave 4 (Age 17): W4SexYP
df$W4SexYP_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W4SexYP, 4)

# Wave 5 (Age 18): W5SexYP
df$W5SexYP_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W5SexYP, 5)

# Wave 6 (Age 19): W6Sex
df$W6Sex_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W6Sex, 6)

# Wave 7 (Age 20): W7Sex
df$W7Sex_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W7Sex, 7)

# Wave 8 (Age 25): W8CMSEX
df$W8CMSEX_h <- harmonize_sex(df$W8CMSEX, 8)

# Wave 9 (Age 32): W9DSEX (no missing codes in metadata, but may have NAs)
df$W9DSEX_h <- df$W9DSEX
df$W9DSEX_h[is.na(df$W9DSEX_h)] <- -3

# Derive consolidated sex variable
# Order: W9DSEX first, then W1, W2, W3, W4, W5, W6, W7, W8 (earliest to most recent among earlier sweeps)
df$sex <- df$W9DSEX_h

# If W9DSEX is missing (-3, -9, -8, -1, -2), fall back through earlier sweeps in order: W1, W2, W3, W4, W5, W6, W7, W8
fallback_vars <- c("W1sexYP_h", "W2SexYP_h", "W3sexYP_h", "W4SexYP_h", "W5SexYP_h", "W6Sex_h", "W7Sex_h", "W8CMSEX_h")

for (v in fallback_vars) {
  missing_mask <- is.na(df$sex) | df$sex %in% c(-9, -8, -7, -3, -2, -1)
  df$sex[missing_mask] <- df[[v]][missing_mask]
  # Check if we've filled all remaining NAs
  if (all(!is.na(df$sex) & df$sex != -3 & df$sex != -9 & df$sex != -8 & df$sex != -7 & df$sex != -2 & df$sex != -1)) {
    break
  }
}

# Create labelled factor for sex
valid_codes <- c(1, 2)
missing_codes <- c(-9, -8, -7, -3, -2, -1)

sex_labels <- c("1" = "Male", "2" = "Female")
sex_missing_labels <- c(
  "-9" = "Refusal",
  "-8" = "Don't know / insufficient information",
  "-7" = "Prefer not to say",
  "-3" = "Not asked at the fieldwork stage / not interviewed",
  "-2" = "Schedule not applicable / script error / information lost",
  "-1" = "Item not applicable"
)

# Combine labels
all_labels <- c(sex_labels, sex_missing_labels)

# Create the labelled factor
df$sex <- labelled::labelled(
  x = as.numeric(df$sex),
  labels = all_labels
)

# Keep only NSID and sex
df_final <- df %>% select(NSID, sex)

cat("Final dataset nrow:", nrow(df_final), "\n")
cat("Sex value distribution:\n")
print(table(df_final$sex, useNA = "always"))

# Write output
write_csv(df_final, "data/output/cleaned_data.csv")
cat("Output written to data/output/cleaned_data.csv\n")

1. **File Loading**

   - Use the exact ID variable name from the source datasets `NSID`.
   - Do not rename the ID variable to a generic name such as `id`.

3. **Identify the Target Variables**
   - Use the additional requirements to identify the construct and required output variable names.
   - Use metadata for the files and the variables to identify all relevant source variables for that construct.
   - If a file is listed in the metadata, load it and include it in the merge frame.

4. **Decide the Output Structure**
   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.

     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.

     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.

   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
